title: 2019 Knox Legal Studies Trial
notes: The question section contains no shared stimuli or figures.

questions.stem:
Brian is spending time in custody awaiting trial.

What is this an example of?

options.B: Remorse
options.C: Retribution
options.D: Recidivism

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a non-government organisation?

options.B: Amnesty International
options.C: The Human Rights Committee
options.D: The International Criminal Court

questions.stem: What feature distinguishes a summary offence from an indictable offence?

options.B: Whether it is a white collar crime
options.C: The number of parties to the crime
options.D: The court which will hear an appeal

questions.stem: Larceny is an example of which category of crime?

options.B: Regulatory offences
options.C: Offences against the person
options.D: Offences against the sovereign

questions.stem: Which of the following is a basic principle of criminal law?

options.B: The right to silence is protected by the Constitution
options.C: Defence must be proven beyond reasonable doubt
options.D: A person charged with a summary offence can insist on having a jury

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of strict liability offences?

options.B: Actus reus must be proven
options.C: Actus reus does not need to be proven
options.D: Both mens rea and actus reus must be proven

questions.stem:
The Crimes (Sentencing Procedure) Act 1999 identifies one purpose of punishment is 'to protect the community from the offender'.

What is this an example of?

options.B: Incapacitation
options.C: Specific deterrence
options.D: General deterrence

questions.stem: What is the main role of the UN General Assembly?

options.B: Settle international disputes
options.C: Address human rights violations
options.D: Preservation of international peace and security

questions.stem:
Louise is 14 years of age and has been accused of committing an indictable offence.

Under the NSW criminal justice system, what rights does she have?

options.A: The principle of doli incapax applies
options.B: Louise cannot be arrested without a warrant
options.C: Louise cannot be charged with a criminal offence
options.D: Louise cannot be incarcerated in an adult prison under any circumstances

questions.answerNote: In NSW the doli incapax presumption covers children aged 10 to 13 only (confirmed by the 2025 DCJ review, dcj.nsw.gov.au), so it does not apply to a 14-year-old; Under-16s are not held in adult prisons, so D is the true statement. A is the alternative if the writer treated the presumption as running to age 14.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the International Criminal Court's (ICC) jurisdiction?

options.A: The ICC has no jurisdiction over war crimes
options.B: The ICC has jurisdiction over all transnational crimes
options.C: The ICC complements rather than excludes existing criminal justice systems
options.D: The alleged crime must be referred to the ICC by the UN General Assembly

questions.stem:
Ross has been accused of committing a crime. He is 12 years of age. The Children's Magistrate has issued a caution.

Which of the following statements is correct?

options.B: Ross pleaded not guilty
options.C: The crime was homicide
options.D: Ross has committed no other offences

questions.stem: Which of the following most accurately defines state sovereignty?

options.B: The authority of a state to govern itself
options.C: The process of formally approving a treaty
options.D: Where a state claims the right to prosecute a person for actions committed in another state

questions.stem: How does protective custody differ from parole?

options.A: Parole is unconditional release of a prisoner; protective custody is conditional release
options.B: The purpose of protective custody is rehabilitation whilst the purpose of parole is deterrence
options.C: Parole is conditional release of a prisoner; protective custody does not involve release of a prisoner
options.D: Parole is a post sentencing consideration; however, protective custody is not a post sentencing consideration

questions.stem:
Jo is 24 years of age. She has been charged with a summary offence and police investigations are continuing.

What protections does the law provide Jo?

options.A: Police may only arrest her with a warrant
options.B: Her silence cannot be used as evidence of guilt
options.C: She cannot be detained in police custody without a warrant
options.D: Police cannot ask her to answer questions for more than two hours without a warrant

questions.stem: Which of the following human rights is best protected in Australia?

options.B: Free speech
options.C: Religious freedom
options.D: Indigenous self-determination

questions.answerNote: Trial by jury has express constitutional recognition in limited federal matters, while other listed rights have more qualified protections.

questions.stem:
Frank is 30 years of age; he has been charged with a crime and the trial process has begun.

Which of the following statements is most correct?

options.A: A ‘guilty plea’ can result in a reduced sentence
options.B: Following a ‘guilty plea’, Frank cannot be granted parole
options.C: If Frank enters 'no plea' this will be recorded as a 'guilty' plea
options.D: A ‘not guilty plea’ may be considered to be an aggravating factor

questions.stem:
Rachel works for Legal Aid; Ben has been accused of a serious criminal matter.

What will Rachel's role be in this case?

options.B: Prosecuting Ben
options.C: Questioning suspects
options.D: Establishing judicial guidelines

questions.stem: How do the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Criminal Court (ICC) differ?

options.A: The ICC is an organ of the UN; the ICJ is not
options.B: The ICJ has jurisdiction over states only; the ICC has jurisdiction over individuals only
options.C: The ICJ was established by the UN Security Council whilst the ICC was established by the Rome Statute
options.D: Decisions by the ICC can be overturned by the United Nations Security Council; this is not the case with the ICJ

questions.stem:
Mary has committed an indictable offence and pleaded not guilty. Her case will go to the NSW District Court.

Which of the following statements is most correct?

options.A: There will not be a jury
options.B: A judge will investigate the case
options.C: Mary's guilt or innocence will be determined by the judge or jury
options.D: The judge may call for evidence that has not been requested by either the defence or prosecution

questions.stem:
The Bail Act 2013 was reformed in 2014 to include show cause.

What are the implications of these changes?

options.A: If the Crown fails to show cause, bail must be granted
options.B: To show cause, the Crown must argue why the detention is justified
options.C: To show cause, the accused must argue why their detention is not justified
options.D: The standard of proof used for making a determination of show cause is beyond reasonable doubt

questions.answerNote: The accused bears the onus of showing why detention is not justified.
